comparator.name: Business Analytics
comparator.sourceNotes: The full-time English 2026–2027 pathway contains 150 EC of compulsory named study and a 30 EC open academic elective/minor period: 60 EC in each year. There is no formal specialization. The adopted regulations and exact annual XB_0112 catalogue require Data Engineering; the recruitment page’s Business Intelligence and Analytics label does not replace that unit. Bachelor Project: Business Case is one 12 EC unit including Study and Career in period 4, Academic Writing in English in period 5 and the company case in periods 5–6. Entry is assessed after December results and requires at least 120 EC, Statistical Data Analysis and Project Big Data. All third-year students take Study and Career; it must be passed before the company case starts. Academic Writing must also be passed before the project grade is awarded. Study and Career requires attendance, assignments, participation and an interview presentation, with compensatory work for notified absence. Writing requires a passed introduction, peer feedback, assignments and attendance at least five of six sessions including both feedback sessions. Teams of at most five submit a joint report/thesis and final product; each student is assessed through observed work, peer reviews, self-reflection and an individual interview. Assessment weights are analytics 20%, synthesis 20%, creativity 15%, initiative 10%, social skills 15%, presentation 10% and writing 10%. The kickoff, project-management workshop, company visit, four presentations and final company presentation are compulsory; workload is at least ten hours weekly in period 5 and full-time in period 6. Thesis and Placement Regulations apply. The English diagnostic test and required refresher are noncredit. First-year BSA normally requires 42 EC, subject to exceptions. Individual open choices need prior examination-board approval, at least 12 EC at level 300 and at most 6 EC at level 100; eligible university/listed minors are exempt. The university Data Science minor is excluded for Business Analytics students; the specified Business Analytics and Data Science minor or Mathematics educational minor are allowed. Foreign study may include one 6 EC master unit that cannot be reused in a later master. Historical transition rules apply to earlier entrants rather than being stacked into this pathway.
components: Open academic elective or minor space
Genuinely open 30-EC academic elective period; minor or approved individual courses, with applicable level rules and examination-board consent.

core: Mathematics, computing and business analysis integrated to improve organizational decisions
Calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics and mathematical optimization for business models
Programming, data management, machine learning and AI for organizational data
Business economics, finance and collaborative applications of analytics
adjacent: Advanced algorithms, computing and mathematical methods for optimization
Customer demand, pricing, finance and organizational strategy informed by analytics
Responsible decisions with business data and artificial intelligence
questions: How can organizations use data and models to improve resource allocation and decisions?
How can demand, pricing and consumer information shape business decisions?
How should organizations use AI and data responsibly?

alternatives.label: Business analytics across mathematics, data and organizations
alternatives.concept: Combines mathematical and statistical methods, programming, data science and AI with economic and business decisions. It approximates VU’s integrated field through UCR courses while lacking its continuous specialist projects and full operations-research sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has substantial quantitative, computational and business study; no one strand alone defines it.
progression: Four planned courses per term, 24 unique courses and eight advanced courses. Personal & Professional Development is in year one. Introductory mathematics precedes the selected courses that require it. Data science and probability precede machine learning.

alternatives.label: Algorithms, AI and mathematical optimization
alternatives.concept: Concentrates on formal and computational methods for business-related decisions, with deeper software development, systems mathematics and reinforcement learning. Business foundations remain as the application setting, while the curriculum gives less room to marketing and organizational study.
alternatives.labelReason: Advanced computing, mathematics and AI occupy the curricular differences from the integrated route.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses differ from the integrated option. Software Development, Linear Systems, Advanced Calculus and Reinforcement Learning deepen formal and computational methods, while the integrated option gives more space to consumer engagement, business AI, market research and advanced algorithms.
progression: Four planned courses per term, 24 unique courses and eight advanced courses. Personal & Professional Development is in year one. Introductory mathematics precedes the selected courses that require it. Data science and probability precede machine learning. Programming and logic precede the spring optimization course. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Econometrics and Psychology of Organizations & Leadership. Advanced Calculus and Reinforcement Learning use their offered final spring.

alternatives.label: Data-informed markets, finance and strategy
alternatives.concept: Uses statistical modelling and data analysis alongside microeconomics, market research and consumer behaviour. Banking simulation, international market-entry analysis and digital strategy add applied decisions about finance, markets and organizations.
alternatives.labelReason: The course set has a substantive business and market sequence supported by data and quantitative methods.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses differ from the integrated option and seven from the technical option. Microeconomics, financial markets, international business and digital strategy deepen the application to firms and markets.
progression: Four planned courses per term, 24 unique courses and eight advanced courses. Personal & Professional Development is in year one. Introductory mathematics precedes the selected courses that require it. Data science and probability precede machine learning.

selection.assessment: The integrated mathematics–computing–business curriculum is the closest feasible UCR response. A deeper algorithmic route and a market/finance strategy route are separately evidenced and differ from each other and from the first route by at least four courses. Responsible AI is recorded as a further target-specific direction, but the three-alternative maximum is reached.

blocks: Both develop accounting and interpretation of financial statements. UCR also introduces costing, budgeting and investment appraisal.
Both develop financial reasoning about risk and the valuation of assets. UCR places substantial weight on banking, monetary policy and bank-management simulation.
Both develop descriptive/inferential statistical reasoning; UCR includes broad research design and group research rather than the complete VU mathematical-statistics sequence.
VU introduces the integrated discipline in a required module. UCR develops its business, mathematics and computing foundations across separate courses.
VU includes an early required analytics project. UCR has course-level research and programming projects with different aims.
VU follows its first analytics project with a second required project. UCR develops project skills across its courses.
VU requires business simulation. The UCR finance option includes a banking simulation with a narrower application.
VU requires a 12 EC company-based team case, with a joint report and product and individual assessment. UCR’s optional independent research has a separate structure.
VU reserves 30 EC for open electives. The displayed UCR plans allocate their credits to the selected themes.
Both develop set-based reasoning. UCR emphasizes logic, induction and proof, while VU also devotes study to combinatorial counting.
UCR search, constraint satisfaction and linear/nonlinear optimization overlap operations-research techniques; the full VU OR sequence remains different.
Both use dynamic programming and network optimization. UCR also studies algebraic algorithms, exact computation and measured performance.
Both develop single-variable calculus. UCR combines differentiation and integration with complex numbers and introductory differential equations.
Both teach systems of equations, vectors, matrices and linear transformations. UCR connects the mathematics to applications such as least squares and principal component analysis.
Both extend the study of calculus. UCR covers multivariable methods and differential equations, with a different scope and sequence.
Both study dynamical systems; UCR focuses on linear time-invariant signals and transforms rather than the full VU dynamics/computation course.
Both study probability spaces, random variables and distributions. UCR also introduces estimation, tests and sampling simulation.
VU requires a dedicated course in stochastic modelling. UCR develops related probability and decision methods across its mathematics and AI courses.
Both teach relational database design and SQL. UCR covers normalization, authorization and query processing.
Both advance software construction beyond introductory programming. UCR uses C++ and Haskell and includes testing, version control and documentation.
Both develop supervised and unsupervised learning and model evaluation. UCR includes practical prediction and method comparison on data.
Both develop programming for computational problems. UCR uses Python and covers control flow, functions, collections, debugging and object-oriented programming.
VU Data Engineering includes building data pipelines and dashboards. UCR introduces data preparation, visualization and databases across separate courses.
VU requires a dedicated Big Data project. UCR uses datasets in several courses, with a different project structure and scale.
VU requires a dedicated Statistical Data Analysis course. UCR develops statistical practice across research methods, machine learning and econometrics.
History of Science is a separate VU requirement.
VU requires a separate Philosophy and Ethics course. The UCR courses on business AI and digital strategy address some governance and responsibility questions.

notes.text: VU Business Analytics requires a substantial sequence in calculus, operations research, statistics, programming and applied projects, including a 12-EC collaborative capstone; its third-year 30 EC elective period remains open. UCR combines related quantitative, computing and business courses, but does not reproduce that full specialist sequence or the VU project structure.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Business Analytics integrates mathematics, statistics, programming and AI to model organizational problems, optimize decisions and implement solutions through a compulsory sequence of applied projects.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three qualified directions in integrated business analytics, algorithms and optimization, and data-informed markets and finance. They combine quantitative methods and computing with business questions in different proportions. VU requires a longer sequence in calculus, stochastic modelling and operations research, and a 12 EC team capstone with a company. Optional UCR independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

curriculum.routeLabel: General Business Analytics, full-time English pathway
curriculum.limitation: The degree comprises 150 EC of required study and 30 EC of open academic electives in year three. Entry to the 12 EC Business Case requires at least 120 EC and passes in Statistical Data Analysis and Project Big Data. Students complete Study and Career before starting the company case and pass Academic Writing in English before receiving the project grade. Teams submit a report and product, with individual assessment. Individually selected electives require approval and must meet level requirements. The English language diagnostic and any required refresher carry no credit.
